Re-sizing Mint partition through Windows or similar..

Mint can read from and write to NTFS partitions, you just need to install the proper software. I believe it's called NTFS-3G. You be able to access it from a base install.

That being said, multiple partitions aren't really necessary for a standard Linux installation unless you plan on re-installing a lot or have special boot requirements. Since I have multiple drives, I usually just erase and use the entire drive when I'm doing an install.

Since you'd rather not reinstall, you might be able to boot into a Mint LiveCD, delete the NTFS partition, and extend the EXT4 partition to cover the remaining space. That's what I'd try to do first. If you can't do that for whatever reason (though it should be possible), you can at least re-format the NTFS partition to EXT4, if you want. You really should be able to just mount NTFS drives in Mint, though...

The easiest way to go about doing what you want is to install gparted in mint and set up your partitions the way you want. After you resize your windows partition it should be flagged for a checkdisk the next time you boot it. If you have windows 8, then you may need to follow this guide if you can't mount it.

I've never heard of the four partition thing before. I don't think it's true, but maybe it's in reference to something else?

I believe the four partition thing is related to the fact that MBR (Master Boot Record) disks can only have 4 primary partitions. This is a limitation of MBR though, not of Linux. Disks with the newer GPT (GUID (globally unique identifiers) partition table) can have up to 128 primary partitions.
Traditional DOS partitioning in the MBR only allows up to four primary partitions. It has nothing to do with Linux.

Sounds like you need to use gparted to reformat your NTFS partition into a Linux friendly format like EXT4, (or FAT32 if you want to also let Windows access it & you won't have files larger than 4GBs on it). Gparted should be on your liveCD, & is also easily installable from the software center.

Would I be able to just format the empty 380GB NTFS partition to Ext4 and use it for my media files like mentioned above?
